PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.ConfigNote: The illustrator's selected surface cues: brick suggested by a few courses where the eye expects them, never every brick. Each pattern is measured in metres on the real surface.

PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.Note: Gauge and Length in metres (a brick course 75 mm, a plain tile's gauge 100 mm); Ink the mark's ink - every mark is drawn with the base pen, 0.13 mm (32__Line__ClassAndPriority/Na__TechnicalPens__Config.json; v0.8.0 took the patterns' own widths away); Perpend how often a joint between units is ticked; Pick how often a unit is picked out with a darker touch of wash; Floor a minimum importance.

PatternsNotes.Rubble: Not courses: laid in groups of stones by PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Rubble__.mjs, from the section below. Gauge and Length are a stone's average, for the sample and the readouts. Ink as Brick's, Adam: 'ensure the linework matches the linethickess and color of the brickwork'

PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.Note: A rubble wall as Vale's illustrator draws it (Thrower, A2Q 15270-1, scanned at 300 dpi and measured): a few groups of stones spaced evenly over a pale wall, each stone two or three broken pen strokes, a loose tan wash dropped in behind. The scans' flicks of white were tried and taken out (Adam: "they do not look good"). Metres on the real surface, so the marks belong to the building and hold still as the camera moves
PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.CellMNote: The wall is divided into cells, offset row by row like bonded stone, each holding at most one group: the 1:50 elevation has about 1.8 stones to the square metre and the perspective about 4; this gives about 3
PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.CellJitterNote: How far a group wanders in its cell, as a share of the cell: enough that no grid shows
PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.GroupShareNote: The share of cells that take a group at Indication 100%, and full size on the sheet
PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.GroupSizesNote: How often a group is one, two, three or four stones: the scan's are mostly pairs
PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.SideBySideNote: How often a group of two lies side by side rather than one over the other: Adam, of columns of stones, 'it spoils the effect'
PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.BondNote: How far a group's upper row sits off its lower, in shares of a stone's width: never straight over it, as a wall's joints never line up
PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.StoneWidthMNote: The 1:50 elevation's stones run about 0.45 x 0.2 m, the perspective's about 0.25 x 0.1 m
PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.GapMNote: Between neighbouring stones in a group: the mortar joint the pen leaves white

Stack.MostNote: No more than this many stones one over another, anywhere on a wall: the next is shifted sideways or left out. Adam: 'make sure too many cant stack vertically ... it spoils the effect'
Stack.GapMNote: Two stones count as stacked when the upper's foot is this near the lower's head
Stack.SharedWidthNote: And when they share this much of the narrower one's width

PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.TiltDegNote: A stone sits this far off level at most
PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.SheetMmNote: A stone's height on the sheet: below the first, no stones are drawn; by the second, all that were chosen

Quiet.PlainNote: A group counts as out on a plain stretch by the share of these probes, this far round it along and up the wall, that find open wall: from none at the first share to wholly at the second
Quiet.KeepNote: Out on a plain stretch a group keeps this share of its chance, wandering between the two over patches this size: the middle of a plain gable goes quiet, as a hand leaves it, while stones gather round corners and openings. Adam: 'see the side looks bad? but the front looks good?'

PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.SheetAspectNote: A stone is drawn only if it comes out at least this many times as wide as it is tall on the sheet. A wall turned away squeezes a stone narrower but no lower, so it comes out square, and twice as close: this thins it as a hand would and leaves a wall seen square on as it was. Adam: 'see the side looks bad? but the front looks good?'
PainterlyNPR__MaterialIndication__Config.OnWallEpsMNote: A stone must lie on its wall in the truth buffer, within this plus a pixel's depth: never across a chimney breast or anything else standing proud of the plane

Pen.TierNote: The base pen, 0.13 mm, as brick courses and every other surface pattern: Adam, 03-Nov-2026, after the structural pen (v0.8.20): 'on the stonework ensure the linework matches the linethickess and color of the brickwork, the line dont feel right on the stone they seem too thick'
Pen.CornerShareNote: A stone's corner radius, as a share of its height: drawn round, as the scan's C-shaped brackets are
Pen.WobbleShareNote: How far the outline strays from true, as a share of the stone's height
Pen.TopGapNote: The pen lifts along the top and the bottom of every stone, for this share of its width: that is what leaves a left bracket and a right bracket
Pen.RightGapNote: And down the right side this often, for this share of its height: the scan's right bracket is often only a hook
Pen.DropChanceNote: A short stroke left out altogether
Pen.TickChanceNote: A dot of the pen beside the right bracket, this often, this long: the scan's ticks and colons

Wash.GroupChanceNote: A broad pale wash loosely round a group, this often
Wash.GroupGrowMNote: How far past the group's stones it reaches
Wash.GroupPeakNote: Its strength, drawn for each group
Wash.LoneChanceNote: A cell with no stones takes a pale wash alone, this often: the scan has a few
Wash.LongAtNote: A wall that comes out this wide on the sheet for its height, or wider, leaves a wash as it is; further turned away, a wash lies longer and lower, so it stays a brush mark rather than a round spot, and fewer groups are kept, in proportion, so they stand as far apart on the sheet
Wash.StoneChanceNote: A darker wash dropped inside a stone, this often: 'the darker washes appear loosely within the bounds of where stones appear' (Adam)
Wash.StoneFitNote: Its size against the stone's: mostly inside, sometimes just over the line
Wash.StoneOffsetNote: How far it wanders from the stone's middle, as a share of the stone: never quite centred
Wash.StoneToneNote: Its strength, drawn for each stone (the scan runs from a pale buff to #D9B27A)
Wash.SecondLobeChanceNote: A second, smaller touch beside the first, so the wash is not a neat oval
Wash.SidesNote: A wash's outline, in straight sides; the shader rags it
Wash.LobesNote: How far the outline swells and falls
Wash.SearchStepsNote: A wash is walked out from its middle this many steps along each side's direction, and stops where the wall does: at a quoin, a window or the wall's own edge
